s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of dyspnea, palpitations, and lightheadedness with ventricular tachycardia
salient_findings: Abrupt onset of dyspnea, palpitations, and lightheadedness
Markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function
key_facts: 66-year-old white man
Presented to the Emergency Department with abrupt onset of symptoms
Found to be in monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
Electrically cardioverted into normal sinus rhythm
Medical history includes cerebrovascular accident, Factor V Leiden and prothrombin gene mutations, hypertension, incidentally noted pulmonary nodules, and chronic kidney disease
Taking losartan and warfarin
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Initial laboratory studies were within normal limits
Coronary angiography ruled out ischemia
Electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm without ischemic changes, but an epsilon wave in V1, a QRS duration of 140 ms, and T-wave inversions in leads V1–V5
Transthoracic echocardiography revealed preserved left ventricular function and no valvular disease, but a markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function

per_call: Myocardial Infarction with Normal Coronary Arteries

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Epsilon wave in V1, QRS duration of 140 ms, and T-wave inversions in leads V1–V5, with markedly dilated right ventricle and severely reduced systolic function

shortlist.label: Cardiac Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Pulmonary nodules and right ventricular dysfunction, with preserved left ventricular function

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical and electrocardiographic features to Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Dysplasia, with right ventricular dilation and dysfunction

shortlist.label: Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia and right ventricular outflow tract dimension >32 mm

shortlist.label: Brugada Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Epsilon wave in V1 and right ventricular dysfunction, although less likely given the absence of characteristic Brugada pattern on electrocardiogram

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, epsilon wave in V1, QRS duration of 140 ms, T-wave inversions in leads V1–V5, and a markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function on echocardiography are consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia.

rejected.label: Cardiac Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While cardiac sarcoidosis is in the differential diagnosis due to the patient's pulmonary nodules, the specific electrocardiogram and echocardiography findings point more towards arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: This is essentially synonymous with arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia and the provided information does not necessitate distinguishing between the two terms in this context.

rejected.label: Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Tachycardia
rejected.why: The patient's presentation with ventricular tachycardia and structural abnormalities of the right ventricle, such as dilation and reduced systolic function, are not typical for right ventricular outflow tract tachycardia.

rejected.label: Brugada Syndrome
rejected.why: While Brugada syndrome can cause ventricular tachycardia, the specific electrocardiogram findings (epsilon wave, QRS duration, and T-wave inversions) and the structural changes in the right ventricle are more indicative of arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia.
